title: Maximum Depth of Binary Tree
statement: Given a binary tree represented as a level-order array where -1 denotes a missing (null) node, return the maximum depth (number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path). Example: tree [3,9,20,-1,-1,15,7] has depth 3. Input is n followed by n integers (level order with -1 for null).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^4, -1000 <= val <= 1000, val != -1 for real nodes (use -1 only as sentinel)

driverCode.python:
##SOLUTION##

import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
i = 0
n = int(data[i]); i += 1
tree = [int(x) for x in data[i:i+n]]; i += n
ans = maxDepth(tree)
print(ans)

title: Validate Binary Search Tree
statement: Given a binary tree as a level-order array with -1 for null, determine if it is a valid BST. A valid BST has all left subtree values < node < right subtree values (strict). Use -1 only as sentinel, real values are not -1.

driverCode.python:
##SOLUTION##

import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
i = 0
n = int(data[i]); i += 1
tree = [int(x) for x in data[i:i+n]]; i += n
ans = isValidBST(tree)
print("true" if ans else "false")

title: Course Schedule
statement: There are numCourses courses labeled 0..numCourses-1. Given prerequisites as pairs [a,b] meaning to take course a you must first take b, determine if all courses can be finished (no cycle). Input: numCourses, m (number of pairs), then m lines each 'a b'.

driverCode.python:
##SOLUTION##

import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
i = 0
numCourses = int(data[i]); i += 1
m = int(data[i]); i += 1
prereq = []
for _ in range(m):
    a = int(data[i]); b = int(data[i+1]); i += 2
    prereq.append([a,b])
ans = canFinish(numCourses, prereq)
print("true" if ans else "false")
